_doc: One entry per independent upstream OmniSeek sends requests to. terms = what the upstream publishes (a number, or 未公布 plus where_checked saying where we looked; url + checked date always). gate = what OmniSeek enforces through the shared BackendGuard (never looser than terms; http_gate false = enforced by the module's own pacer). terms.robots_crawl_delay_s = the Crawl-delay a host's robots.txt sets for User-agent *; each such host gets its own gate (one request at a time, starts at least the delay apart), taken after the upstream gate so the stricter always holds (driver decision, 2026-09-29). terms.max_concurrency 1 also makes the shared http clients use a no-keep-alive HTTP/1.1 transport and send Connection: close for that upstream's hosts. user_agent = the User-Agent the upstream's policy requires: every shared egress layer sends exactly this string to the entry's hosts (redirect hops included) and the shared browser refuses them; the one place it is written (driver decision, 2026-09-29). hosts = exact host names; an entry that starts with '.' is a domain suffix and matches every subdomain of that domain, not the bare domain (list that on its own); for one host a gated entry wins, then an exact entry, then the longest suffix (driver decision, 2026-09-29). disabled = OmniSeek does not send to this upstream: {reason, source, checked, ...}; the code that would send reads it, sends nothing and reports the reason (driver decision, 2026-09-29). pending = a published value not enforced yet and why. A new source must be listed under an existing upstream's sources (or backends) or get its own entry: tests/test_upstream_limits.py fails otherwise. Terms research: task R, 2026-09-28; robots sweeps 2026-09-28.
